summary: This is a web application that converts Excel table data into Markdown format. When users copy a table from Excel and paste it into the textarea, the app automatically formats it as a Markdown table and renders an HTML preview using Bootstrap styling. It's a single-page application built with Vue.js that handles the conversion and display in real-time.

explanations.5: This tells PHP to enforce strict type checking, meaning variables must match their declared types exactly—it catches type errors early.
explanations.28: This creates a constant called 'REPO' that stores the GitHub repository URL, so it can be reused throughout the code without hardcoding the URL multiple times.
explanations.32: This checks if a template file called 'octocat.tmpl' exists in the current directory; if it does, the code reads and processes it.
explanations.33: This reads the template file's contents and replaces the placeholder '%REPO%' with the actual GitHub repository URL stored in the REPO constant.
explanations.86: The v-model directive two-way binds the textarea to the Vue component's 'editor' data—any typing updates the data, and vice versa. The @change and @paste handlers trigger functions when the user modifies the content.
explanations.89: The v-if directive only renders this section if the 'Markdown' variable contains text, so it stays hidden until the user actually pastes data.
explanations.106: Math.max.apply is being used to find the longest string in a column of data—'apply' lets you pass an array as arguments to the Math.max function.
explanations.115: This splits the pasted data by line breaks (handling multiple line break formats) and then splits each line by tabs, creating a 2D array where each sub-array is one row of the table.
explanations.134: This pads each cell with spaces so all cells in a column have the same width, making the Markdown table visually aligned.
explanations.143: The splice method inserts a new separator row (made of dashes) at position 1 in the array, which is right after the header row in Markdown table format.
explanations.179: This creates a new Vue instance that manages the entire app—it connects to the HTML element with id 'app' and controls all the data and interactivity.
explanations.191: event.clipboardData gives access to what's currently in the user's clipboard when they paste.
explanations.202: The marked() function converts a Markdown string into HTML—in this case, the Markdown table becomes an HTML table element.
